packets.implementation:
All in closeout.py, no change to the gate scripts (PROOF.2 adds their re-judge).

(1) THE DIGEST. One `git ls-tree -r -z --full-tree HEAD` read per close-out -> {path: blob}. A gate's digest is sha256 over the sorted `<path> <blob>` lines of the paths its input set selects, then the gate's env lines. Reuse needs a clean tree (the existing dirty gate, closeout.py:380-385, with gate-record moved out of the tree it stays meaningful), so HEAD's blobs are exactly what the gate reads. Input sets, read from what each gate runs (each set is a function of `cargo metadata --format-version 1 --locked --offline`, the resolve graph; at BASE the closures hold 35 (glia-engine with its dev-deps), 38 (glia-cli) and 37 (glia-py) of the 40 workspace packages):
  CODE(root) = the directories of the workspace packages in root's dependency closure (normal + build deps; the root's own dev-deps too, since tests and examples link them) + Cargo.toml + Cargo.lock + every tracked path an `include_str!` / `include_bytes!` in those directories names outside them (scanned, so rank_eval's `../../.glia/overlay.toml` and the tests' bench/substrate-gap/fixtures/.. includes are found, never listed by hand).
  - tests (`cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast` + `--test byte_identical`): the whole tracked tree EXCEPT `dev-notes/` (closeout.py itself re-added: see (4)) and `bench/` other than `bench/substrate-gap/` (minus its outputs results-latest.json, legacy-latest.json, COVERAGE.md, results.jsonl), `bench/doc-link/` and `bench/edge-audit/`. The broad set is deliberate: cli/tests/readme_surface.rs reads README.md, cli/tests/skill_surface.rs reads skills/, code-domain tests include docs/overlay.md, engine/tests/self_scan.rs copies every tracked file outside its SKIP (bench/, dev-notes/, tests/, ..) and builds it. Env: `rustc -Vv`, `cargo -V`, sha256 of the local untracked .cargo/config.toml (mold, debug level).
  - fmt: every tracked `*.rs` (engram-export's included) + rustfmt.toml; env `rustfmt --version`.
  - rustdoc: CODE of every workspace package + Cargo.toml + Cargo.lock; env as tests. Only a FULL (`--workspace`) green run is recorded and only a full need reuses it; a partial (touched crates) run is never recorded.
  - rank (measure): CODE(glia-engine, dev-deps included: rank_eval is its example; glia-embed's worker is in the closure) + scripts/rank-gate.sh + bench/rank-gate/snapshots.json + bench/rank-gate/gate.json WITHOUT its `accepted` key (canonical JSON of the rest: the trim reads `rankers` / `items`); env: rustc, the FASTEMBED_CACHE_DIR listing (file names + sizes). rank (judge): bench/rank-gate/baseline/** + gate.json `accepted`. The rank digest is measure + judge.
  - cohort (measure): CODE(glia-cli) + scripts/cohort-gate.sh + bench/cohort/ minus results/ + bench/sibyl/; env rustc. cohort (judge): bench/cohort/results/baseline/**.
  - wheel (maturin build + install + api surface + message-contracts + pyo3 surface tests): CODE(glia-py) + CODE(glia-cli) (message-contracts runs `cargo run -p glia-cli`) + bench/message-contracts/; env `maturin -V`, LEAP_PY's `-V`. Reuse also needs the INSTALLED wheel to be the recorded one: the venv's glia_py .so sha256 and `build_stamp()` equal the record's (else rebuild).
  - bench (run.py + matrix + test_matrix + test_grade): the installed .so sha256 (its code input) + bench/substrate-gap/ minus its four outputs; reuse also needs the four outputs at HEAD byte-equal to the ones the recorded run wrote (sha256 in the record), since the commit carries them.
  - engram: not recorded (1 s with its own build cache; it also reads the sibling ../Engram, outside this tree). It always runs.
  Pinned by a test: GATE_PATHS['rank'] (RANKED_PATHS) and GATE_PATHS['cohort'] (COHORT_PATHS) are each inside their gate's measure set, so a gate a packet touched can never be reused.

(2) THE RECORD. `~/.cache/glia-closeout/gate-record.json` (override GLIA_CLOSEOUT_RECORD), on /home so a reboot (which clears WF=/tmp/..) and a `git checkout dev-notes/wave-runner` between attempts cannot drop it; logs copied to `~/.cache/glia-closeout/logs/<gate>-<digest12>.log`. Schema 1: `{schema, gates: {<gate>: {green: [<entry>, ..last 8], last: <entry>}}}`, entry = `{digest, measure, judge, tier: "full" | "partial:<labels>", ok, line (the gate's last marker), lines (the `== ..` lines it printed), commit, tree, wave, release, at, log, outputs: {path: sha256}, so_sha256, stamp, env_fail: bool}`. Written after EACH gate finishes (green -> `green`; any result -> `last`), so a later gate's failure keeps an earlier gate's green for the re-run. Atomic write (tmp + rename).

(3) THE DECISION, per gate, before running it: `fresh` if GLIA_CLOSEOUT_FRESH (`all` or a comma list of gate names) names it, or `--fresh <gates>`; else reuse the newest green entry whose digest equals HEAD's and whose tier covers the need (a full entry covers a partial need; a partial entry covers only the same labels or a subset; a full need takes only a full entry). The need is today's: the release's last close-out (`remaining` empty) and a FULL_GATES_EVERY wave need full; a mid-release wave needs the fast tier (RANK_FAST / COHORT_FAST) unless a packet touched RANK_CODE_PATHS (rank full) as today. Reusing a full entry when full was due sets gates_last_full[g] = wave (nothing a full run would read has moved since it passed). The mid-release `skipped - wave touched no ranked path` / cohort `skipped - wave touched no ..` lines are REPLACED by reuse: a gate whose inputs did not move since a green run is reused; one whose inputs moved runs, whoever moved them (hole (1)). With no record at all (the first close-out after this packet), today's touched-based skip applies once, printed `(no record yet)`. Print one line per gate: `[closeout] reuse <gate> from <commit12> (wave <w>, <tier>, digest <12>)`, followed by the recorded `== ..` lines re-printed with a ` (reused <commit12>)` suffix, or `[closeout] run <gate> (<reason>)` with reason one of `forced`, `no record`, `inputs moved: <n> paths (<first 3, from git diff --name-only <recorded commit> HEAD filtered by the gate's set>)`, `env moved: <rustc|rustfmt|maturin|python|fastembed|cargo-config|installed-wheel|outputs>`, `need full, record partial`, `last result FAILED`.

(4) closeout.py ITSELF: the sha256 of closeout.py is an env line of every gate (a change to how a gate is run invalidates every record); the rest of dev-notes/wave-runner/ (schedules, baseline.json, briefs) is not an input.

(5) THE RELEASE SET. When `remaining` is empty every recorded gate (tests, fmt, rustdoc, rank, cohort, wheel, bench) must be fresh-full or reused-full at HEAD's digest, plus `rank-gate.sh coverage` (always run: it reads gate.json only). One line: `[closeout] set tree=<HEAD^{tree} 12> fresh=<a> reused=<b> full=<k>/<n>` and, per gate, `<gate>=<fresh|reused <commit12>>` in the commit body. A partial or skipped entry never completes the set; GLIA_COHORT_GATE_SKIP at the release stays a failure.

(6) RATCHETS. The rank and cohort ratchets (closeout.py:662-678) run only when that gate ran FRESH and FULL in this close-out and everything is green (today's rule plus `fresh`). A reused full gate prints `== [<gate>-gate] ratchet: skipped - reused from <commit12>; GLIA_CLOSEOUT_FRESH=<gate> to ratchet`. (The scripts' own HEAD guards already refuse a ratchet from a check made at another HEAD.)

(7) [gate-asks] (GP.12). gate_result() gains the reused form: the attribution line reads `== [gate-asks] <gate> result=ok reused_from=<commit12> asked_by=<n> (<ids>) touched_by=<m> (<ids>)`. An ask never forces a fresh run by itself (the inputs decide; a packet whose acceptance names a gate but touched none of its inputs is answered by the reuse, and the line says so); touched_by > 0 with a reuse is impossible by (1)'s pinned subset and is asserted (a failure, `reuse with touched paths`).

(8) TMPDIR (memory: the 0.5.6 release's full cohort hit `Disk quota exceeded (os error 122)` on /tmp's 25.6 GB user quota). sh() sets TMPDIR for every subprocess to CLOSEOUT_TMP = $GLIA_CLOSEOUT_TMP or ~/.cache/glia-tmp when the caller's TMPDIR is unset or resolves under /tmp (an explicit /home TMPDIR is kept); mkdir -p; one line `[closeout] tmpdir=<dir> free_gb=<f>` at the start (the /home 40 GB check at 397-402 covers it). TMPDIR is in no digest (results do not depend on it). A gate whose log, or the cohort gate's scratch results (${GLIA_COHORT_GATE_DIR:-~/.cache/glia-cohort-gate}/run/**/*.jsonl, *.log), carry `Disk quota exceeded`, `os error 122`, `No space left on device` or `os error 28` is recorded `env_fail: true`: its entry is never green, the gate line gains ` (environment: <signature>)`, and PROOF.2 never re-judges from it.

(9) THE BASELINE WRITES (hole (2)). baseline.json (612-625) and LANDED (627-637), and the `schedule --verify` / gen_wave steps after them, run only when `gates` is empty; on a failure the record (2) holds what passed and the tree stays as the close-out found it (corrections folding at 583-610 is unchanged: it is idempotent and already filtered).

(10) READ-ONLY MODES. `closeout.py --digests` prints, without running anything, one `[closeout] digest <gate> measure=<12> judge=<12> files=<n> env=<12>` per gate at HEAD; `--plan-only` (existing) also prints each gate's decision (`[closeout] plan reuse <gate> from <c>` / `plan run <gate> (<reason>)`).

(11) RELEASES gains the 0.5.7 key ("057") and its packet-id prefix in RELEASE_PREFIX if the integrator's schedule packet has not added them (one line each; the integrator names the prefix).

(12) README.md: a 'Gate reuse' paragraph (the digest sets, the record path, GLIA_CLOSEOUT_FRESH / --fresh, the release set, the ratchet rule, TMPDIR).

Four new DocRefusal reasons, checked in resolve_doc_mention for the bare-name tiers (2/3) only; a qualified (tier 1) mention is unchanged. (1) Position (D4). The 24 bytes before the span on its line, lowercased and trimmed, end with one of the words `rule`, `rules`, `key`, `keys`, `field`, `fields`, `kind`, `kinds`, `kinds:`, `gains`, `flag`, `column`, `marker`, `emitter`, `variant`; or the span's line holds a `[[]]` stanza name before it; or the span itself holds `": ` / `{` (a JSON-shaped span); or the word right after the span is one of `key`, `field`, `rule`, `kind`, `cell`, `flag`, `column`. Refusal `Position`. (2) Private (D4). A candidate that is a FUNCTION / METHOD whose POSITION file ends `.rs` and whose CODE text (leading `#`-attributes and `///` lines skipped) does not start with `pub ` (`pub(crate)` / `pub(super)` count as private) is eligible only for a doc under the same deepest PROJECT root as the candidate. With no other eligible candidate: refusal `Private`. (3) Other project (D5). A doc whose deepest project root is a sub-project (DocCtx.root is Some and not the repo root `""`) binds a bare mention only to a candidate under that root; when every eligible candidate is outside it: refusal `OtherProject`. Root-level docs (README.md, docs/ at the repo root) keep FD.79's behaviour. (4) Chord (D6). The span is joined to a neighbouring span by ` + ` ("`Alt` + `Tab`", "`Ctrl`+`K`"): refusal `Chord`. packets.title: ASP.NET: a template-less verb attribute (`[HttpGet]`) beside an action's `[Route("t")]` constrains that route's verb instead of minting its own `GET <controller prefix>` route: `[HttpGet][Route("apps/{app}")]` is one ROUTE `GET /apps/{app}`, not `GET /` plus `ANY /apps/{app}` (also fixes the HTTP_CALLS `any` pairing to a PUT / DELETE-only template)
packets.rationale: BASE 57b0e22c. HC.3 held-out panel (confidence-gate-0.5.7.md item 4a, HANDLED_BY|fact under floor; and the above-floor HTTP_CALLS|derived 10/11 note). Wrong verdicts, squidex@f828dd717edc: 00b4588f57e712b5 `GET / @backend/src/Squidex -HANDLED_BY-> Squidex::Areas::Api::Controllers::Schemas::SchemasController::GetPreviewUrlsCompletion`, parser:csharp, site SchemasController.cs:376: 'GetPreviewUrlsCompletion serves GET api/apps/{app}/schemas/{schema}/completion/prview-urls ([Route] beside [HttpGet]); no GET / route exists'; 01beee55da2cde04 `endpoint:GET:/api/apps/${…} @frontend -HTTP_CALLS-> ANY /apps/{app}/ @backend/src/Squidex`, resolver:http rule any: 'the GET /api/apps/{name} call is served by [HttpGet][Route("apps/{app}")] GetApp; the apps/{app}/ template paired here carries only the PUT and DELETE actions'. One cause, by symbol: parsers/code/csharp/src/lib.rs `check_route_attrs` loops over `own_attributes(node)` and emits one ROUTE per attribute: `[Route(t)]` -> `ANY <prefix>/t`, and a verb attribute with no template (`[HttpGet]`) -> `<VERB> <prefix>` (with no controller `[Route]` the prefix is `/`). ASP.NET Core's attribute routing (DefaultApplicationModelProvider selectors) reads them as one route: a verb attribute without a template is only an HTTP-method constraint applied to the action's template routes; it is a route of its own only when the action has no template-bearing attribute. So every squidex action written `[HttpX]` + `[Route("..")]` (the whole API, 54 controllers) gives one bogus `<VERB> /` ROUTE shared by every such action in the repo, and its real path as verb-less `ANY`, which resolver:http pairs by rule `any` to whichever ANY template matches (PutApp / DeleteApp's `apps/{app}/`). Size: full squidex: `GET / @backend/src/Squidex` HANDLED_BY 108 actions, `POST /` 54, `PUT /` 60, `DELETE /` 31 (253 false HANDLED_BY|fact), and 207 `ANY /..` ROUTEs in *Controller.cs files. A second reader already works around it: parsers/code/extractors/src/openapi_annot.rs `handled_routes`' 'Precision guard' refuses to key an op on the `GET <prefix>` half of the pair and 'keys by itself once the parser composes the pair' (squidex: `[openapi-annot] .. ops=4 unkeyed=201` summed over the build). True cases kept and pinned: `[HttpGet("{id}")]` under a controller `[Route]` (fixture csharp-aspnet-composed, test `aspnet_relative_template_composes`), bare `[HttpPost]` inheriting the controller template (`aspnet_bare_verb_attribute_inherits_prefix`), absolute `[HttpDelete("/admin/..")]` (`aspnet_absolute_action_template_overrides_prefix`), a lone `[Route]` action staying ANY, the controller's own ANY route (`aspnet_full_methods_and_route_attr`).

Composition: an opaque record's own path is `/~<head>` joined with `tail` (normalised); `is_route_path` is applied to the path with the `~<head>` segment removed (the head is identifier bytes and `.` only, sanitised and clipped to 64 bytes). The cause is v0.4.13's `collect_self_attr_assignments` (parsers/code/python/src/lib.rs), which turns EVERY `self.<attr>` attribute node in a method body into an ATTRIBUTE via `emit_class_attribute`, reads included (on purpose: marshmallow's metaclass-set `Schema.opts`, pinned by `class_attribute_emits_has_attribute_edge`). Reads also mint: (a) the class's own methods (`self.render(..)` mints ATTRIBUTE `render` beside METHOD `render`, same qname), (b) inherited members (`self.repos`, `self.assertEqual`, `self.request`). Measured at BASE on mealie's Python tree: 3513 HAS_ATTRIBUTE edges, of which 388 name a METHOD the class itself DEFINES, 253 a METHOD of an INHERITS_FROM ancestor and 554 an ancestor's ATTRIBUTE. DECISION (asked: should only an assignment declare, and not even one to a base's property?): (1) an assignment `self.X = ..` (also augmented, tuple / list target, `for self.X in`) declares X: Python creates an instance attribute unless X is a data descriptor on the type; (2) a class-level `X = ..` / `X: T` declares X (unchanged); (3) neither declares when X is a METHOD of the class itself (a property's assignment calls its setter; a read of a method is the method, already a node); (4) a read-only X (never assigned in the class, not class-level) declares X only when the class names no base other than `object` / `ABC` / `Protocol` (a subscript base like `Generic[T]` is not recorded as a base today): with a real base the name is presumed inherited (or set by the base's metaclass) and belongs to whoever declares it. That keeps the rule's reason for reads (the base-less metaclass-attached `Schema.opts`) and drops the audit's false edge. NOT decided in the parser: an assignment to a property an ANCESTOR declares in another file (a setter call, no attribute) - the parser cannot see it; it stays an ATTRIBUTE (residual, see questions). Every rule is parser-side because a Python class body is one file (own methods and bases are read where the class is), so no graph-side node removal and no GA.3 / watch fast-path surface change.
